record.title: compactness lemma
record.name: CompactnessLemma
record.content:
An immediate consequence of the definition of a compact object $X$ of an additive category $\mathcal{A}$ is the following lemma.
{\bf Compactness Lemma}
An object $X$ in an Abelian category $\mathcal{A}$ with arbitrary direct sums (also called coproducts) is compact if and only if the functor $hom_{\mathcal{A}}(X,-)$ commutes with arbitrary direct sums, that is, if $$hom_{\mathcal{A}}(X,\bigoplus_{\alpha in S} Y_{\alpha}) = \bigoplus_{\alpha \in S} hom_{\mathcal{A}}(X,Y_{\alpha})$$.
{\bf Lemma}. Let A be a ring and M an A--module. (i) If M is a finitely generated A--module, then M is a compact object of A-mod. (ii) If M is projective and is a compact object of A--mod, then M is finitely generated.
{\bf Proof.}
(i) follows immediately from the generator definition for the case of an Abelian category.
To prove statement (ii), let us assume that $M$ is projective, and then also choose any surjection $p : A^{\bigoplus I}$ \to M, with $I$ being a possibly infinite set. There exists then a section $s : M \to |A^{\bigoplus I}$. If M were compact, the image of $s$ would have to lie in a submodule $$A^{\bigoplus J} \subseteq A^{\bigoplus I},$$ for some finite subset $J \subseteq I$. Then $p|A^{\bigoplus J}$ is still surjective, which proves that $M$ is finitely generated.
